seo.title: Weddings & packages — Rosewood Courtyard
seo.description: Wedding packages for the 2027 season at Rosewood Courtyard, from an intimate elopement at £4,800 to a two-night grand celebration, with in-house catering.

props.heading: One wedding a day, and it is *yours*
props.subheading: Exclusive use of a walled garden, a kitchen that cooks from it, and a coordinator who knows every brick.

image.alt: Bride holding flowers in warm evening backlight

props.heading: Unhurried, generous and quietly organised
props.body:
We cap the season at ninety weddings so that every couple has the full attention of the team. Your coordinator will meet you at least three times before the day, and stays until the last carriage leaves.

Our kitchen cooks everything on site. Menus change with the garden — asparagus and elderflower in May, heritage tomatoes and peaches in August, venison and quince in October.

We welcome your own suppliers for flowers, music and photography, and are happy to introduce people we trust.

props.heading: Choose your *starting* point
props.subheading: Prices include VAT, exclusive use, your coordinator and our in-house catering. Everything can be adjusted.

items.title: Intimate Elopement

image.alt: Couple’s hands with rings beside a bouquet

items.description: A short, beautiful ceremony in the Rose Courtyard, photographs in the garden and a long-table supper in the Orangery.
inclusions: Glass of English sparkling wine on arrival
Bridal bouquet from the estate beds
The Bridal Loft for the night
items.validity: Valid for the 2027 season, April – October

items.title: The Courtyard Day
items.priceNote: Up to 90 guests, Friday or Sunday
items.description: Ceremony among the roses, drinks on the lawn and a wedding breakfast by the fire in the Coach House — with every bedroom for the night.
inclusions: Evening food and late bar until 11pm
items.validity: Valid for the 2027 season; Saturdays from £19,500

items.title: The Grand Celebration

image.alt: Banquet table set with flowers and glassware

items.description: The whole estate from Friday afternoon to Sunday brunch: welcome supper, the wedding itself and a long, lazy morning after.
inclusions: Ceremony, reception and dinner in the Orangery
Evening food, late bar and DJ booth
Two nights in the Coach House

props.heading: How a Rosewood day *unfolds*
props.subheading: A typical summer Saturday — every timing can move to suit you.

items.title: Morning in the Bridal Loft
items.text: Hair, make-up and breakfast brought up from the kitchen while the team dresses the courtyard.

items.title: Ceremony among the roses
items.text: Guests gather on the gravel paths; the registrar stands beneath the old pear tree.

image.alt: Rings resting on roses before the ceremony

items.title: Drinks on the lawn
items.text: English sparkling wine, elderflower spritz and canapés from the garden, with lawn games for the children.

image.alt: Bartender pouring an amber cocktail for the reception

items.title: Wedding breakfast
items.text: Three seasonal courses in the Orangery or the Coach House, followed by speeches as the light softens.

image.alt: Guests sharing the wedding breakfast at a long table

items.title: First dance & evening guests
items.text: The Orangery doors fold open, the band starts and the festoon lights come on across the courtyard.

items.title: Carriages
items.text: Music ends at 11pm. Twenty-four lucky guests walk upstairs; everyone else is waved off under the stars.

props.text: Not only weddings: we host a handful of anniversaries, renewals and milestone birthdays each season, with the same care.

items.quote: Clara, our coordinator, answered every one of our 214 emails with the same patience. On the day we didn’t make a single decision.
items.author: Priya & Sam

items.quote: The food was the thing our guests still talk about — the lamb, the late-night toasties, the strawberries from the walled garden.
items.author: Rosa & Daniel

items.quote: We eloped with twelve people and it never once felt small. Just intimate, and entirely ours.
items.author: Ama & Lewis

props.heading: Wedding questions
props.subheading: More detail on our full FAQ page, or ask your coordinator anything.

items.question: How far ahead should we book?
items.answer: Summer Saturdays in 2027 are booking now, typically 14–18 months ahead. Weekdays and shoulder-season dates are often available within six months.

items.question: What deposit is required?
items.answer: A 25% deposit secures your date, with the balance due eight weeks before. Payment plans are available on request.

items.question: Can we have a marquee?
items.answer: Yes — The Lawn takes marquees of up to 400 guests. We work with two preferred marquee companies and can share quotes.

items.question: Do you offer menu tastings?
items.answer: Every couple is invited to a tasting for two in the Coach House around six months before the wedding.

props.heading: Let’s find the *right* day
props.subheading: Tell us your season and your numbers, and we’ll reply with availability within one working day.
